text: Ridgeline Outfitters runs order-service, a checkout API on AKS that today emits only unstructured print lines -- no timestamp discipline, no request correlation, nothing a query engine can filter on. This lab turns that into a real instrumented service: structured logs, a custom metric, and a trace span, all wired into Azure Monitor and correlated by the same request ID.

Step one replaces print statements with a JSON log formatter that carries a request_id and order_id on every line, the pattern Chapter one described and Lesson two built in detail. Every call site passes those values through extra, so filtering Log Analytics on one request_id returns every log line that belongs to one specific checkout -- a real ground-truth lookup instead of scrolling raw text.

Step two records an order_checkout_duration_seconds histogram with OpenTelemetry, because AKS's built-in CPU and memory metrics can't see inside the request. Step three wraps only the risky payment-gateway call in its own trace span, nested inside the checkout request's parent span, so a slow charge_card call shows up exactly the way Lesson one's inventory-service example did -- as the dominant child span.

Wiring it all into Azure Monitor takes one call at process startup: configure_azure_monitor, pointed at the Application Insights connection string from Chapter two. From that single call, the structured logs, the checkout histogram, and every charge_card span all flow through the same pipe, tagged with the same trace context -- no separate exporter configuration for each signal.

Verification is one KQL query across AppTraces, AppMetrics, and AppDependencies, filtered to a single OperationId -- Application Insights' name for the shared trace ID. It returns the log line, the histogram recording, and the charge_card span for one real checkout, in order. That shared ID, not any one pillar in isolation, is the actual proof this lab worked.

order-service now emits all three pillars for every real checkout, correlated by one ID instead of living as three disconnected streams. Lesson 30 moves from observing behavior to observing cost -- building a real dashboard grouped by tag and a budget alert, so a spend problem gets caught as early as a reliability problem now does.
